generations.prompt: Night on the stone balcony; the camera is locked off, level with the young woman in the pale gold gown, who leans on the balustrade on her folded forearms, chin on the back of her hand, the white earbud in her left ear, her phone glowing on the stone by her elbow; vertical frame. Without changing her bored posture she speaks down to the courtyard, the words lovely and fluent, exactly these: "Were I the dawn, I would come an hour early, and apologise to no one." As she finishes she stifles a yawn behind her hand. Then she straightens up and looks down at him properly, curious, for the first time. She is the only person in the frame and the only one who speaks. The camera does not move. Sound: her voice clearly, crickets; no music. No on-screen text, no captions, no lettering anywhere.
